runs.question: Under Northbridge University's guidance, may faculty enter Level 2 research data into the university's approved AI assistant?

answer.text:
The documents give two answers that conflict, and neither one says which governs.

**Yes, according to the IT standard.** The Office of Information Technology's Generative AI Use Standard (IT-STD-114) names Northbridge AI, the university's enterprise generative AI assistant, as the approved tool for university work. Under its data rules, faculty, staff and researchers may enter data classified up to Level 2 (Moderate Risk), including unpublished research data, into Northbridge AI.

**No, according to the research guidance.** The Office of Research's guidance (OR-GUID-27) takes a stricter line. It says that research data classified above Level 1 (Public) must not be entered into any generative AI tool, including university-licensed tools. Its stated reason is that sponsor agreements and data use agreements often restrict where data may be processed. It adds that generative AI services may log prompts outside the systems those agreements cover.

**Status of the conflict.** Both documents are dated effective September 1, 2026, and both apply to all faculty, staff and researchers. Neither refers to the other, and I found no passage saying one overrides the other. For Level 2 research data, the research guidance's ban on any generative AI tool is the more specific rule for research data. Still, I can't confirm that from the documents, so I'd treat the question as unresolved until the Office of Research or the IT Service Desk confirms which rule applies. The research guidance directs questions to the Office of Research Compliance.

Both documents are also marked "SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT," so you may want to check them against the official university versions before relying on them.
